findings.title: clamp marks exact floor and ceil values as out of range
findings.cause: The boundary checks use <= for floor and >= for ceil even though the docs describe clamping only when the number is smaller than floor or larger than ceil, and the docstring example expects an exact ceil value to format without the token.
findings.impact: Values exactly on accepted thresholds are displayed with '<' or '>' warning tokens, so threshold UI, reports, or metrics can falsely label in-range values as under or over limit.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:509-514 uses inclusive comparisons
src/humanize/number.py:473-476 documents clamp(0.99, ceil=0.99) as '99%' and clamp(0.999, ceil=0.99) as '>99%'
tests/test_number.py:223-240 covers below and above but not equality
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
assert humanize.clamp(0.99, format='{:.0%}', ceil=0.99) == '99%'
assert humanize.clamp(0.01, format='{:.0%}', floor=0.01) == '1%'
PY

findings.title: intcomma leaves negative numbers ungrouped
findings.cause: After coercion, the formatter repeatedly applies a regex anchored to leading digits only. A leading '-' prevents the grouping substitution from ever matching.
findings.impact: Negative integers and negative decimal amounts are returned without thousands separators, unlike positive values and unlike other public number functions that intentionally preserve negative signs.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:164-174 formats the string with r'^(\d+)(\d{3})'
tests/test_number.py:41-83 has no negative intcomma cases
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
assert humanize.intcomma(-1234567) == '-1,234,567'
assert humanize.intcomma('-1234567') == '-1,234,567'
PY

findings.title: fractional loses or duplicates the sign for negative fractions
findings.cause: The function truncates with int(), computes a negative fractional remainder, then either abs() hides the numerator sign for values between -1 and 0 or emits a negative numerator in the mixed fraction.
findings.impact: Negative values are not data-preserved: -0.3 becomes positive and negative mixed fractions render as malformed strings such as '-1 -1/2'.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:370-382 computes whole_number, frac, numerator, denominator and uses abs(numerator) only in the no-whole-number branch
tests/test_number.py:166-189 covers positive fractions and non-finite values but no negative fractions
probe: fractional(-0.3) -> '3/10'; fractional(-1.5) -> '-1 -1/2'; fractional('-8.9') -> '-8 -9/10'
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
assert humanize.fractional(-0.3) == '-3/10'
assert humanize.fractional(-1.5) == '-1 1/2'
PY

findings.title: time humanizers crash on float infinity
findings.cause: The numeric coercion paths catch ValueError and TypeError, but int(inf), round(inf), and datetime.timedelta(seconds=inf) raise OverflowError.
findings.impact: Non-finite numeric inputs can raise instead of returning a stable string, which is inconsistent with the documented naturaldelta fallback for inf/nan and with the number-formatting functions' explicit non-finite handling.
evidence: src/humanize/time.py:113-116 says non-convertible inf/nan values are returned unchanged
src/humanize/time.py:149-153 catches ValueError and TypeError around int(value)/timedelta only
src/humanize/time.py:87-90 and src/humanize/time.py:534-536 route naturaltime/precisedelta through _date_and_delta with the same missing OverflowError handling
tests/test_time.py:130,181,230 cover string 'NaN' but not math.inf
probe: naturaldelta(math.inf), naturaltime(math.inf), and precisedelta(math.inf) all raise OverflowError

findings.title: metric does not promote rounded 1000 mantissas
findings.cause: The SI prefix is selected from the pre-rounded exponent and the formatted mantissa is never rechecked when it rounds up to 1000.
findings.impact: Boundary values violate the precision contract and produce awkward lower-prefix output such as '1000 k' instead of promoting to the next SI prefix.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:570-583 chooses exponent/prefix before formatting value_
src/humanize/number.py:547-551 says the prefix avoids non-significant zero digits and the precision argument controls the number of output digits
tests/test_number.py:243-309 lacks 999.x and 999999-style promotion boundaries
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
assert humanize.metric(999.9, 'Hz') == '1.00 kHz'
assert humanize.metric(999999, 'Hz') == '1.00 MHz'
PY

findings.title: translation coverage can pass while all locale binaries are missing
findings.cause: The repository contains .po files but zero .mo files, the build config only includes existing .mo artifacts, and the i18n tests skip on FileNotFoundError instead of failing when catalogs are absent.
findings.impact: The advertised non-English locales are unavailable in the current checkout, and CI can report a green test suite with localization effectively untested and broken for users unless an external release step happens to compile catalogs.
evidence: find src/humanize/locale -name '*.mo' | wc -l -> 0
pyproject.toml:53 lists build.artifacts = ['*.mo'] but no build hook compiles them
scripts/generate-translation-binaries.sh:3-7 is a manual compiler script
tests/test_i18n.py:36-37,68-69,87-88,166-167,188-189,199-200 skip on FileNotFoundError
uv run --extra tests pytest -q passed with 685 passed, 69 skipped
probe: activate('fr_FR'), activate('ru_RU'), activate('de_DE') each raised FileNotFoundError
findings.reproduction_or_test:
find src/humanize/locale -name '*.mo' | wc -l
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
humanize.i18n.activate('fr_FR')
PY

findings.title: naturalsize lacks non-finite input handling
findings.cause: The function converts to float and immediately uses abs/log without checking math.isfinite, unlike the number module's public formatters.
findings.impact: NaN inputs raise ValueError and infinity is rendered as a maximum-suffix filesize, which is surprising and inconsistent for a public numeric formatting helper.
evidence: src/humanize/filesize.py:89-101 converts value to float, computes log(abs_bytes, base), and indexes a suffix without a finite guard
tests/test_filesize.py:12-88 covers finite positive and negative values only
probe: naturalsize(math.nan) raised ValueError; naturalsize(math.inf) -> 'inf QB'
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import math, humanize
assert humanize.naturalsize(math.nan) == 'NaN'
assert humanize.naturalsize(math.inf) == '+Inf'
PY
